archetypes.name: breaking-contracts
archetypes.rationale: release-prepare.sh changes WARN→ERROR (exit 0→1) for unmatched commits and ci_monitor.py adds a 3600s blocking wait for in_progress CI — both are behavioral contract changes with deployment risk worth dedicated review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the behavioral contract changes in this diff. In `.claude/skills/release/scripts/release-prepare.sh`, the previous behavior emitted a `WARN:` and exited 0 when commits outnumbered PRs; the new code exits 1 with `ERROR=unmatched-commits` for any commit not resolvable to a PR — assess whether operators with squash-merge workflows lacking `(#N)` subjects will be silently broken by this change and whether the new `UNMATCHED_COMMITS` exit-1 path interacts correctly with the `emit_error` helper and the downstream SKILL.md consumer. In `python/ci_monitor.py`, the new `_wait_for_ci_ready` function polls up to `CI_MONITOR_IN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` (3600 s) before returning — check whether there is an interrupt/signal path, whether the `ci-still-in-progress` → `Outcome.OK` return in `monitor()` prevents the outer loop from cycling indefinitely when CI stays perpetually in-progress, and whether the new `clock` parameter is threaded through every call site. Also verify that the `config.py` constants `CI_MONITOR_IN_PROGRESS_POLL_INTERVAL` and `CI_MONITOR_IN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` are appropriately sized and documented. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scope-drift
archetypes.rationale: _render_ship_pr reads CI_PASSED/FAILED_RUN_ID/STALL_STEP/BAIL_REASON/MERGE_RESULT — five fields beyond the plan spec — and _last_artifact recurses the entire tmpdir; both warrant a focused architecture pass.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review `python/progress_report.py` for scope and design concerns not covered by correctness or edge-case passes. The plan spec for `_render_ship_pr` names only `PHASE`, `PR_NUMBER`, `PR_URL`, and `ITERATION`, but the implementation also reads `CI_PASSED`, `FAILED_RUN_ID`, `STALL_STEP`, `BAIL_REASON`, and `MERGE_RESULT` — confirm whether these extra fields are justified and whether they create an implicit contract on `ship-pr-state.sh` key names that could break if that file evolves. Inspect `_last_artifact` which performs a full `os.walk` of the tmpdir on every `p` invocation — assess whether this could be slow on large runs and whether it respects symlinks or could escape the tmpdir. Check that `_review_rounds_root` and `_current_round_dir` use consistent path roots (implement_tmpdir vs. larch-logs subdirectory) as described in the plan. Verify that `_render_step5` actually shells out to `render-review-phase-detail.sh` as planned, and that subprocess failure correctly falls back to `_render_generic`. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
